speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has been a very busy year for Singapore on the foreign and global stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee, who by the way has just returned from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, suggested that I address Parliament because after all, foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is essential that all of us are privy to all the activities that we have been conducting, and I will be happy to take questions from Parliamentarians after this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have witnessed – in fact, we are witnessing – a global order in very rapid transition.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is marked by big superpower rivalry, rising protectionist sentiment, xenophobia and, in the midst of all this, an ongoing technological digital revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small country, we have to respond, and we have to respond nimbly in a very volatile global environment, we have to make ourselves relevant to all powers big and small, and we have to enlarge, to the maximum extent, the political and economic space for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To this end, Singapore has worked very hard to make progress on several diplomatic and economic initiatives, and we have redoubled our efforts to support a rules-based world order and also to buttress the international trading system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This year also happened to be the year that Singapore chaired ASEAN, and we had, therefore, to host a large number of regional and international events.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to thank all those who have been working so tirelessly over the past year, and especially our staff from the Civil Service, entire Government as well as the private sector and, of course, our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Without this whole-of-Nation effort, we could not have achieved all that we have achieved this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As well as them, we also had Leaders from the United States (US), Russia, China, India, Japan, the Republic of Korea (ROK), Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Chile.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition to that, we also had Ms Christine Lagarde, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We sought to strengthen ASEAN's Unity and Centrality and, in particular, to turn challenges, existential challenges into opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And that is why, during this year, when we were ASEAN Chair, we focused especially on enhancing ASEAN Centrality, unity and coherence; second, to accelerate ASEAN's economic integration; and third, on equipping people throughout ASEAN with the skills needed for new jobs in the digital revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members can see that actually we have focused very much obviously within Singapore on SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But in fact, this is a need in all countries – skills for new jobs in the digital revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Furthermore, we have also sought to enhance interoperability of digital and trading systems within ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have also asked the Clerk to distribute an infographic which summarises the variety of initiatives that we launched this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst it is circulating, let me continue to address all Members.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Strengthening a rules-based world order has been key to regional security and peace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, it is this post-World War II liberal economic global environment and adherence to a rules-based multilateral system that have given us peace for 70 years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And, in particular, created enormous opportunities for a tiny "red dot" like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, this remains a constant focus for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are the world’s first multilateral guidelines to manage unintended encounters between military aircraft.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will make for a safer and more secure aviation environment in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Terrorism and cyberattacks are, unfortunately, a clear and present danger.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We enhanced regional counter-terrorism cooperation through the "Resilience, Response and Recovery" Framework and we also held a Symposium on a Collective Approach to Counter-Terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In August, we completed our three-year term as the ASEAN-China Country Coordinator.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members will appreciate that this is, in fact, a very sensitive and very difficult issue that we have been grappling with for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And not just us because, in fact, we are not a claimant state, but four ASEAN members are claimant states that have overlapping claims with China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fortunately, we have witnessed patient, meticulous diplomacy and all the parties involved – China and ASEAN – have been able to lower temperatures, and we have been able to work constructively.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also brokered an ASEAN consensus on an ASEAN-China Maritime Exercise after nearly three years of discussions, and we co-directed this exercise with China last month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the economic front, ASEAN has stood against the tide of protectionism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We made substantial progress on the negotiations for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: RCEP includes the 10 ASEAN countries and includes the other six which are China, Japan, ROK, India, Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This network will create a common framework for smart city development and the mutual exchange of action plans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The network will also connect cities with external private sector partners which will enable us to co-develop solutions for sustainable urbanisation, and members will appreciate that sustainable urbanisation is another mega-trend of our time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Collectively, these efforts will ensure that ASEAN remains vibrant, dynamic, relevant and will create bountiful opportunities for our businesses and our citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also contributed to regional humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And perhaps at this juncture, I should say a few words about the humanitarian situation in Rakhine State.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I visited both Bangladesh and Myanmar earlier this month, and I also made a trip to the refugee camps in Cox's Bazar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was shortly after both countries had announced their intention to commence the process of repatriating a first wave of refugees.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I must say that, based on my own observations at the camp, the Bangladesh government has actually done a really admirable job of providing humanitarian assistance for a very large number of refugees in a very short order of time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But having said that, having also visited the camps, the current situation is unsustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As long as the refugees remain in the camps, and have no jobs and means of livelihood, they will have no future prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Therefore, we have to welcome the fact that both Myanmar and Bangladesh are engaged in direct, detailed discussions on making preparations for the commencement of repatriations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is not a complete solution and there are many, many details that still need to be sorted out.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Nevertheless, we do need to witness the commencement of a process and to make sure it is done in a way that provides for the refugees to return in a safe, secure and dignified way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The situation in Rakhine State is of concern to all ASEAN member states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the 33rd ASEAN Summit last week, all ASEAN Leaders discussed how ASEAN can support the efforts of both Myanmar and Bangladesh for the safe, voluntary return of refugees.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We welcomed Myanmar’s commitment to ensure the safety and security of all communities in Rakhine State.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN stands ready to support efforts by all parties to address the root causes of the situation in the Rakhine State.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fundamentally, race, language, religion continue to remain live issues in our region and, indeed, across the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ultimately, it is the responsibility of the Myanmar government and its respective stakeholders to find a viable and durable long-term political solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And as I have said before in this Chamber, we cannot expect quick fixes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Twenty-eighteen has also been about bringing ASEAN to our young people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, we organised the first-ever ASEAN E-sports and music festival, we renewed the Singapore-ASEAN Youth Fund, and we launched the ASEAN Youth Fellowship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These schemes provide for shared experiences of sportsmanship, community service and entrepreneurship, and we hope that this will spur more youths to get involved in ASEAN activities and strengthen our ASEAN Community and, ultimately, even more important, to strengthen the ASEAN identity amongst young people across Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our Chairmanship this year has been a whole-of-nation effort and it involves, as I said earlier, all Government agencies, our media, universities, think tanks, the private sector and the non-government organisations (NGOs).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN has given us a collective platform to improve the lives of our citizens, and make our voices heard on the world stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Post-2018, Singapore will continue to play the role of "Shepherd" for the ASEAN Smart Cities Network, and we will continue to bring new ideas to the table.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is still much more that ASEAN can achieve, and we will work with our counterparts to build a more united, resilient and innovative ASEAN in the years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN remains a cornerstone of our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, our standing as a trusted partner on a global level.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There were at least two events which reaffirmed our reputation as an impartial, reliable and capable partner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Much has been said about the Summit, and I do not want to go through all that again.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And so, we are proud that it went well, and that we had played a small part in easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, if Members just cast your minds back a year ago, the situation was extremely tense, rife with fiery rhetoric and provocative actions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we hope that, given time and further negotiations and constructive diplomacy, there will be sustained peace and stability, and a fully denuclearised Korean Peninsula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our region, and indeed the world, will be much better off for it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Another event that I want to highlight more recently is the Bloomberg New Economy Forum.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members may be aware that, in fact, China was originally supposed to host this Forum, but when that did not materialise, Bloomberg had to relocate the event very, very urgently.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, over two days in the first week of November, we witnessed the arrival of global business and political leaders gathered in Singapore to discuss the challenges confronting the world economy and possible solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Bloomberg founder and former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg, Chinese Vice President Wang Qishan, and former US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger were all in town in that week.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They joined some of the many other luminaries who came to attend the Forum.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We were happy to be able to facilitate and to participate in these important discussions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And it is in our interest to add value and to make ourselves relevant to the global business community.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Overall, both these major events enabled us to raise our standing in the world and fly our flag high.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Malaysia, we have had a positive momentum of high-level exchanges with the new Pakatan Harapan government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We just hosted Prime Minister Mahathir to an Official Visit last week, and our leaders will meet again next year for the annual Leaders' Retreat.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My Cabinet colleagues and I have built good rapport with our new Malaysian counterparts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia has a new, diverse and lively Cabinet – in fact, their ages range from 25 to 93 and I think that is a world record – but we do share many aspirations and challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I can speak certainly for the younger Ministers, both in Singapore and Malaysia, that there is good rapport, there is good communication, we are all on Whatsapp and various other digital means of communication.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I can assure Members that we are not revealing state secrets!

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But nevertheless, that ability to communicate instantly, quickly and appropriately helps to build trust.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Issues will inevitably arise from time to time in our relations, and we will seek constructive ways to resolve them, while firmly protecting our national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On fundamental issues, and one key fundamental issue is the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On this case, our position is clear, consistent and has been articulated on many occasions, including in the Prime Minister's National Day Rally speech and, in fact, in my own Parliamentary Statement in July this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am glad that both sides followed due legal process and put the matter to rest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The significance of that date is that it will be exactly two years from when the new government took over in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We did so in a spirit of bilateral cooperation and goodwill and, at the same time, protected our interests and rights under the Bilateral Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Overall, the outcome was balanced and reflected both countries' commitment to uphold agreements and to advance bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Indonesia, our relations are in good shape, underpinned by the robust and expanding economic cooperation, for example, in projects like the Kendal Industrial Park in Central Java and the Nongsa Digital Park in Batam, which, in fact, I launched with Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi in March this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The highlight of the year was the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat in Bali last month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was, in fact, the Prime Minister's third Retreat with President Joko Widodo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These agreements reflect our belief that Indonesia's economic fundamentals are strong and that Indonesia is a large and dynamic market, with many opportunities for Singapore businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a fellowship scheme to deepen ties between Singaporean and Indonesian regional leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We wish Indonesia smooth elections in I believe April next year and look forward to continuing our mutually beneficial cooperation with them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 2018, we also reaffirmed our special and longstanding relationship with Brunei.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, President Halimah made her first State Visit to Brunei in May 2018 at the invitation of His Majesty the Sultan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Earlier this month, we also welcomed His Royal Highness Crown Prince Billah and a delegation of Bruneian Ministers for the sixth edition of the Young Leaders’ Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a key programme that enables the younger leaders on both sides to deepen personal ties and enhance trust and confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides have maintained a steady cadence of high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This year, Prime Minister Lee, Deputy Prime Minister Teo and Deputy Prime Minister Tharman have all visited China; whilst on their side, Premier Li Keqiang, Vice President Wang Qishan and Vice Premier Han Zheng have also visited Singapore in recent months.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to build on our deep and substantive cooperation with China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will enhance bilateral economic cooperation between China and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also made good progress on all three Government-to-Government projects, the Suzhou Industrial Park, the Tianjin Eco-City and the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative (CCI).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, there is a new acronym in town.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was formerly called the Southern Transport Corridor.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The CCI-ILSTC connects the overland Silk Road Economic Belt with the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It will enhance infrastructure connectivity and commerce within China, and between China and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, one of the reasons for the name change – and this suggestion came from China – was to make the point that they are talking about bilateral two-way flow of goods and services between China and Southeast Asia, and obviously we are at the heart of Southeast Asia and, from there, to connect to the rest of the Maritime Silk Road.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Cooperation on the Belt and Road Initiative is a new highlight of our bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has progressed well under the four platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, infrastructural connectivity; second, financial connectivity; third, opportunities for third-party collaboration; and fourth, professional services, including legal and judicial cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There will be much work to pursue in the years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will build on this year’s strong momentum to further enhance our bilateral cooperation with China, including at the provincial level, through the latest proposed Singapore-Shanghai Cooperation Council.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It spans defence, economic, security, education, scientific and people-to-people spheres.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This year, we enjoyed a broad slate of high-level, substantive bilateral exchanges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: President Trump was here in June, Vice President Mike Pence last week, and earlier in August, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Secretary of Defence James Mattis was here for the Shangri-La Dialogue and National Security Advisor John Bolton was here last week as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Several Ministers, including me, have visited the US this year to meet our counterparts and engage members of Congress.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Prime Minister has spoken with President Trump on several occasions on the telephone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have expanded bilateral collaboration in new and emerging areas, such as tax information exchange, cybersecurity, financial technology (fintech), e-commerce, infrastructure development, smart city solutions, advanced manufacturing and robotics, and technology partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The current Administration may have a different approach to trade, but the fundamentals that undergird our longstanding relationship with the US remain strong.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US remains committed to our region, and we will continue to do more with the US Administration in the years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the United Nations (UN) General Assembly this year, I spoke about the crisis of confidence in multilateralism and its institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I also made clear that Singapore will double down on our support for multilateralism and the rules-based global world order.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In a sense, we have no choice but to subscribe to that because we will always be a small, tiny red dot, and our trade volume is more than twice our gross domestic product (GDP).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we have no choice but to subscribe and do our best to support multilateralism, a rules-based world order and international trade.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Keeping a free and open trading framework and having recourse to third-party dispute resolution mechanisms are essential for a tiny city-state like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have done our bit to help shape international norms on emerging new areas with transboundary impact, for instance, cybersecurity, climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have thus maintained our advocacy for Singapore's interests in international organisations, such as the UN and the World Trade Organization.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA has also been closely supporting the Ministry of Trade and Industry's (MTI's) efforts to advance our agenda of free trade and economic integration.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also just concluded the 3rd Review of the Agreement between New Zealand and Singapore on a Closer Economic Partnership (ANZSCEP).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, the FTA with New Zealand was one of our first-ever bilateral FTA for both of us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For those of you who do not know, MERCOSUR includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we are also in the midst of negotiating an FTA with the Pacific Alliance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Pacific Alliance is Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MERCOSUR and the Pacific Alliance are significant trading blocs in South America.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Again, for those who do not know, the EAEU includes Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and Kyrgyzstan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should make a shout out to Koh Poh Koon, who has been making a lot of trips to that part of the world, which many Members may not be familiar with.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also played an active and constructive role at APEC and the Group of 20 (G20).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I told Members that the Prime Minister just returned last night from Papua New Guinea and we will soon be going to Argentina as well for the G20 meeting.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On this trip, I will have to drag along Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat and I must tell Members, for those of you who really want to go, it will take you at least 30 hours to reach Buenos Aires and another 30 hours to come back.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, in conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker and Members of this House, we recognise the uncertainty and volatility in today's world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But if we look at what has been achieved this year, we do not need to be pessimistic about its outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Trusted by our neighbours and by the international community.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They trust us because they know we are straight, honest brokers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are sticklers for international law, a rules-based world order and free trade, and we believe in the sanctity of agreements and contracts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And they also trust our competence to be able to deliver when times are short and the outcomes are urgent and important.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to be nimble to adapt, seize opportunities and to do our best.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA will work closely with all other Ministries and agencies to keep our foreign policy balance sheet in good order.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What is important – and this is a point I want to re-emphasise – is that foreign policy begins at home and we do need to maintain broad domestic support for our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: An effective foreign policy rests on this domestic consensus, a consensus built both within this House, and outside this House with fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As we commemorate our Bicentennial next year, 2019, I hope Members will continue to work as a whole-of-Nation, to build a safe, secure and prosperous home for all Singaporeans and our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Building a rules-based region and bringing our economies closer are key and relevant initiatives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are talking about a current and still evolving situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I said earlier, the silver lining, having visited both Bangladesh and Myanmar and having spoken to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh and the State Counsellor of Myanmar, is that I can state with a fair amount of confidence that both sides sincerely do want a return of the refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The State Counsellor herself has acknowledged that they are residents of Myanmar and that they are entitled to go back.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a brave position for her to take.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, Bangladesh, as I said earlier, has done a fantastic job, a really admirable job, in looking after the refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But they also know that it is not sustainable and that, at some point, the refugees need to go back.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has to be voluntary, it has to be safe, and it has to be dignified.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I cannot give Members a very specific date on which it will actually begin.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because apart from the preparations made by both sides, the refugees themselves have to agree and have to want to go back.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having spoken to some of the refugees, the refugees' key concern is security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having to risk life and limb to get across to the refugee camps, their question is: will it be safe for me to return?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: How will my neighbours, the community and the other communities in Rakhine State view their return?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They have asked what will be their livelihood?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because, in the end, nobody wants to be a refugee.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Everyone wants to get a job, a good job, to be able to support their families.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the point is that there are many, many details that need to be sorted out.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other point I would emphasise is that the UN High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) and the UN Development Programme (UNDP) also have to do their part, both in terms of support and presence on the ground but also in building confidence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should bear in mind that there are extremists on both sides who do not want this problem to be resolved and do not want the refugees to go back early.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because as long as this problem remains unresolved, it is a festering locus for extremism and for the recruitment of future terrorists.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Which, ultimately, threatens not only their immediate neigbourhood but, in fact, threatens us all, across ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, there are a lot more details that need to be sorted out.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What I can say now, from my own interactions, is that there is sincere goodwill on the part of both Myanmar and Bangladesh.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And, of course, as ASEAN, we will also be willing to step up.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And it is ultimately about confidence and trust.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the domestic lesson for us here is to understand why we are so focused on making sure inter-ethnic and inter-religious relations are looked after so assiduously.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because once those ties, the fabric, is torn, it is very, very difficult to put together again.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Deputy Speaker, I have one clarification for the Minister concerning our relationship with Indonesia, particularly on the issue of extradition.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I believe about a decade ago, the Singapore and Indonesian governments agreed to tie extradition together with some defence cooperation agreements, and, we have noted the Minister's update that we have concluded an ASEAN model Extradition Treaty.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, my question is: how will this model treaty affect our position with Indonesia as far as extradition is concerned?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does it mean that the Singapore Government is prepared to proceed on extradition without it being tied to defence cooperation?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is a good question, and I thank the Member for asking that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What I referred to was the ASEAN Model Extradition Treaty which, in a sense, forms a starting base to begin negotiations for an ASEAN Extradition Treaty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Being a lawyer, you know that once it becomes regional, the scope and conditions will be quite different from that of a bilateral treaty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I would still keep this on two separate channels.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The important point for the ASEAN Extradition Treaty is that we do want to emphasise the importance of rule of law and interoperability within ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I would not conflate the two Extradition Treaties, because we are going to keep them separate.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The specific terms and conditions will not be the same between the two.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As a lawyer, the Member would know, for instance, if you want to extradite someone, you have to show that it is an offence on both sides domestically.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I want to emphasise that it is on different terms.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, on the issue of refugees, I am glad that the Minister said that ASEAN countries should step up.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Could I ask what kinds of specific help, financial or otherwise, other ASEAN countries, other than Myanmar, have pledged to assist to resolve the crisis?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: And have any countries agreed to take in some of the Rohingya refugees selectively?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, there has been a global outpouring of support for the refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I believe Senior Minister of State Maliki was there at the handover.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Specifically, within Myanmar itself, when they go back – I myself have not visited Rakhine State – but the reports that I have received were that a lot of the homes and the farms were destroyed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Thay actually need to rebuild homes and a means of livelihood.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But actually, what is important is for the refugees themselves to be able to construct homes of their design and at the standard they are accustomed to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But actually, my sense of the issue right now is that the primary limiting factor is not money.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The primary limiting factor is trust – confidence on the part of refugees and trust, and the ground conditions within Rakhine State itself.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we, as ASEAN, should be prepared to help in whichever way possible.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And sometimes just the delivery of humanitarian assistance on the ground and having people on the ground – it is not so much the specifics of what is in the package – but the fact that someone else was there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Someone else was there in goodwill and helping to build trust.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is another point I want to emphasise.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You must remember that there are other minorities within Rakhine State.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, the indigenous people in Rakhine are the minority in Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, trust requires all communities to be confident and to have a hope that there is a better future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is a lot more work to be done.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I just wanted to clarify a little bit on the point that Ms Sylvia Lim raised.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Defence Cooperation Agreement and the Extradition Treaty that we signed with Indonesia – it was signed by both governments.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And in the Minister's opinion, how far is the draft away from being adopted by all the member states?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Yes, it is true we have arrived at a single Draft Negotiating Text.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But let me not raise false hopes that all the issues are simple to resolve.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For instance, if you speak to the different claimant states, each of them will stand up and loudly proclaim, "Those areas are indisputably mine".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In other words, even what is in dispute is disputed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do Members see my point? "This is indisputably mine." Then another side picks it up and say, "No, this is indisputably mine".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You cannot even agree on what areas are in dispute.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am just giving Members an example of a very thorny issue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Other thorny issues: is this a binding agreement?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And then there are enough lawyers here who may quickly then ask: is this a legally binding agreement?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And then for those Members who are familiar with international law: even if you get a judgment, how will it be enforced?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am just trying to give Members a flavour of the enormous challenges which lie ahead.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My own view is that that is a very optimistic scenario.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I said earlier, the fact that patient, meticulous and constructive diplomacy has at least brought us to this point where the waters of the South China Sea are much calmer is still worth noting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But do not ever assume it is going to be an easy or short journey.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It is important for us to stand up for multilateralism at a time when nationalism is on the rise everywhere.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The question I have relates to some of the issues that arose from the SingHealth enquiry.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Do we still have to worry about foreign interference in our local politics?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And if so, what could be the best steps our people could take to prepare to deal with that?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member's second question was what steps we need to take.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first point is public education and people need to be aware that we will always be a target for campaigns and misinformation campaigns and deliberate online falsehoods.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the first thing is to be aware of it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point is to be sceptical of what you receive through all your social media feeds.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I remember this very good piece of advice that our former President Dr Tony Tan gave.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: He said when you receive a message, ask who it is from; second, ask who it will benefit and, of course, ask if it is accurate or not.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to prejudge other issues which will be brought to this House.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There will always be the danger of foreign interference.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You will have to take it almost as standard statecraft of the digital age.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if you assume everyone is going to act with restraint, it will be very foolish.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, I previously asked the Minister whether Singapore will be sending a second consignment of humanitarian aid to the Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh and the Minister at that point, replied that it is pending further assessment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Now that he has been to the refugee camps, could I ask for an update on whether we will be sending these humanitarian supplies?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second is on the repatriation, which I agree should happen.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I am wondering whether once they are back in Rakhine state, whether there are plans to grant them citizenship.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because as the Minister mentioned, we have to address the root causes, and one of the root causes of why they fled and resulted in this crisis is because they did not have citizenship.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And the third is in the repatriation process, whether there will be UN peacekeepers on site.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think that was one of the requests of the refugees, to ensure that this repatriation is both safe and secure for them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What I saw in the refugee camps in Cox's Bazar – I know the Member was there, but he was there earlier last year – and according to the people on site, there is a vast difference now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The conditions the refugees are living now are much much better than when they first arrived.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You know, I used to be the former Environment Minister, so I notice things like drains, latrines, water supply, food supply, cooking gas and energy, and actually there has been a lot of work that has been done, especially on the Bangladesh side of it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My greater concern will be when they return – the rebuilding programme and, ultimately, their livelihoods and making a living.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I really do not want to get into the issue of citizenship because that is not for us, the Parliament of Singapore, to be debating or to decide on behalf of Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is something which they have to sort out through their own political processes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, this issue of UN peacekeepers is a sovereign issue that has to be sorted out by Myanmar and, if I were Myanmar, I would be offended if a Parliament elsewhere were making pronouncements on such issues.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, with your permission, I am not going to get into those two specific issues.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Always think about how we, in Singapore, would view others pontificating or prescribing how we should solve our own political problems.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If I may add on another achievement for 2018, it is also Singapore Parliament hosting the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), where we had the opportunity to discuss many issues, like deepening regional economic integration, and also meet with many new Members of Parliament, including those from Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And whether during the ASEAN Leaders Summit, does the Minister sense the political will to conclude the RCEP?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And the final point is to assure the Minister that as he represents Singapore in the various places, including Argentina, his Group Representation Constituency Members of Parliament stand ready to cover his duties when he is not around.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I must tell Members I travel almost as much as a cabin crew.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I calculated, I took about 36 visits a year, so I thank you for your personal support.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, I should start off with an apology to the House for not mentioning AIPA meetings which the Member has hosted, and Speaker has chaired.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has also been particularly eye-opening for the younger Members of Parliament to meet your counterparts from other ASEAN states and, more importantly, to see how these issues can paralyse us, can divide us and how difficult it is.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I mean there were some resolutions that you cannot even get onto the agenda, much less agree on a resolution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I want to congratulate and thank all Members who did participate in AIPA, and I encourage you to continue participating as it moves on to other destinations as well.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are a couple of both negotiating as well as political considerations which have led to the current position where we can report substantial progress but not yet conclusion.
